goal: Transportation Company — design doc build order steps 1-4
strategy:
Driven by one mechanical fact and one judgement.

The fact: builders run in parallel and pieces must be file-disjoint. Seven concerns touch public/index.html (OPS_ECON, OP_LABELS, the duplicated opNiceName map, _opAfterFound, the new window.MythicTransportBridge block, _ppGenListing's haul roll, the launcher tile, the script tag). They collapse into ONE piece (8), which also owns version.txt and sw.js because CLAUDE.md's deploy triple must move together or the update check breaks. Piece 8 is large but unavoidable, and it has the strongest available bar: index.html's own exemplar hunks.

The judgement: seams fall where a critic can judge the artifact WITHOUT the rest of the feature. Each remaining piece is one file with a type-matched exemplar from this repo's ratified best work, so a blind A/B is meaningful — catalog vs catalog (rigs.data.js vs production.data.js), bridge vs bridge, pure-and-total vs tiers.js, renderer vs production.render.js, money/failure-envelope vs cost.js, derived-state vs production.state.js, migration vs sql/015. I deliberately did NOT bar contracts.js against community.api.js nor index.js against city/index.js even though those are the closer functional analogues: neither is in the ratified BAR list, and cost.js / community.bridge.js test the properties that actually matter here (atomic spend + refund closure; NULL_BRIDGE key-for-key parity).

REJECTED DECOMPOSITION #1 — split by the doc's build order (SQL / rigs+PP / depot+charter / exchange). Wrong cut: steps 2, 3 and 4 each touch index.html, so every step collides with every other on one path, violating file-disjointness outright. It also produces pieces judgeable only in context ("step 3" is half a legacy hunk plus half a catalog).

REJECTED DECOMPOSITION #2 — one "module" piece for all of public/src/transport. It hides the six distinct disciplines the BAR exists to test (a Supabase guard envelope and a pure pricing function have nothing in common) and gives the critic a 900-line diff with one bar_file. Worse, the two files most likely to be wrong — the bridge and the SQL — would be buried.

REJECTED #3 — a separate piece for index.js (registration/overlay/bind). It has no type-matched bar left in the ratified list once the other six are assigned, and it is thin glue over pinned signatures. Folded into piece 3 with transport.bridge.js: both halves of the seam land in one change, which is itself the rule the bar states.

NOT BUILT IN THIS RUN, and each piece is told so:
- Step 5, battle integration. ZERO change to _vmResearchMult (index.html:195451) or playerOwnsVehicle (195441). The flat 1.4→1.9 clamp raise is the named landmine; the haul-only branch belongs to step 5. transport_rigs.assigned_to ships as a labelled dead hook in SQL only.
- Step 6: escorts, region tolls, convoy raiding, frConvoyIntercept extension.
- §8.1 making _jbConvoys() stateful. ZERO change to index.html:218953. PHASE = 1 only, with the ≥3-carrier / ≥5-carrier promotion criteria written beside it as a comment.
- Phase 2's Hand-hauled penalty (35% cargo / +25 risk / 1.6× trip) and Phase 3's hard gate.
- Multi-slot lot footprints. lotSlots is authored as data and explicitly NOT enforced: one-vehicle-one-slot is an invariant in ~12 sites and only the buy path was ever going to be changed. Recorded as a rejected design with its cost.
- The Antitrust event (§5.4), the used-rig P2P extension (_vmCreditSeller is a documented no-op), a PP "Fleet tab" inside renderPrincePortfolios, and any Forge-flagged pure-monopoly mode.
- _convoyCanSend / _convoySpend / CONVOY_TRUCKS / GARAGE_RIG_FX / worker.js: untouched, verified by grep.

bar.why_it_is_the_bar: The ceiling of the SQL series and probably of the repo. It is a migration that reviews itself. (a) It opens by stating its own STATUS honestly — "🔴 THIS FILE HAS NEVER BEEN RUN" — and says exactly what applying it does and does not achieve. (b) It contains a named postmortem of the revision it replaces: the r9 settle function inserted the client payload verbatim, and two HTTP calls minted a billion Cinder; a negative `spillover_payout` permanently poisoned a rival's `sum(amount)` in a table with no UPDATE path to correct it. The fix (§4 bounds sign, address, magnitude, arity) is described in terms of that attack. (c) It states the LIMIT of its own guarantee under the heading "⚖ THE LIMIT OF WHAT A SERVER CAN CHECK HERE, stated plainly rather than implied" — node-city's world is a client blob, so the server can bound a settlement but not recompute it, and "Do not read this file as claiming otherwise." (d) It kills a policy rather than commenting an intent the mechanism cannot express: "POSTGRES RLS HAS NO COLUMN GRANULARITY… The comment described an intent the mechanism could not express" — and then `revoke update … from anon, authenticated` "so the denial does not depend on this policy staying deleted." (e) Mutual RLS recursion between two tables is diagnosed and solved with definer helpers scoped to the caller's own question, with the r9 over-broad helper cited as the counterexample. (f) The verify query ends with a NEGATIVE assertion (`no_upd = 0`) and a warning that a previous revision asserted a count it never ran. (g) It even scopes its own claim about `service_role` and BYPASSRLS.

The compact canonical migration; 110 lines with nothing wasted. Header is THE BUG / THE FIX / 🔒 SECURITY REVIEW, and the bug is described from the player's seat ("An owner who accepted two players saw neither of them, and had no way to tell whether it had worked"), not as a stack trace. The security review is a five-bullet argument, each bullet naming an attack it closes: pinned `search_path` because "a caller could shadow `public` and run their own tables as the owner"; the founder check read fresh inside the function against `corporations` — "Read it fresh; never trust input" — with the RPC taking only a request id so it "cannot hire into a corp you do not found, cannot invent a user_id, and cannot promote anyone to founder." It also documents a deliberate NON-enforcement with a business reason: the member cap is not checked server-side because "over-cap hiring is a paid action the client already charges Aza for, and duplicating the rule server-side would silently void a purchase." Retry safety is explicit (double-click / dropped connection returns the existing membership). It ships a bounded backfill that can only touch rows a founder already approved, and its verify is a per-corporation data-state report with a stated pass condition: "`stuck_hired` must be 0 for every row."

The reference statement of the append-only rule, and the source of the sentence the rest of the repo quotes: "There is no balance column, because a balance column is a thing that can drift from its own history." It also pre-empts the obvious wrong reading of itself — "⚠ This ledger records CONTRIBUTION. It is deliberately NOT a second wallet sitting beside corp_treasury" — and says where the money actually leaves the player. Two lines carry the whole security argument: the INSERT policy pins `user_id = auth.uid() and kind = 'contribution' and amount > 0 and is_community_member(...)` under the comment "Without the amount check, a member could post a negative row and delete the community's recorded history by arithmetic"; and then "APPEND-ONLY, enforced rather than asserted. No update or delete policy exists and the grants are revoked" — belt and braces, so a later migration's permissive policy cannot silently reopen history. It is idempotent throughout and ends with a counted verify (`expect tables 2, policies 3, rpc 1`).

Best example in the repo of a fix argued from production evidence rather than from theory. The header reframes the bug as a wrong QUESTION ("season_apply suppresses a directive only for a user who ALREADY TOOK IT. That is the wrong question"), then pastes five real account fingerprints — five directives applied within one minute, each ending on zero Cinder — as the evidence. "🔴 WHY THE GATE LIVES ON THE SERVER, NOT IN THE CLIENT" quotes the client code it is protecting and makes the killer point that a client-side fix cannot reach old cached builds, "which matters because the players being hurt are by definition the ones whose install is out of date." It ships TWO gates and says they are separate "because they fail differently" (72h expiry vs account-age, the latter unconditional). It explains a counter-intuitive return value — `already:true` rather than `ok:false`, because `ok:false` would make the client re-fire the RPC on every 120s poll forever. And it guarantees reversibility: "⚠ NOTHING IS DELETED", with a new nullable `skipped_reason` column plus a `comment on column` so the audit trail can distinguish a row that wiped somebody from one that did not.

The best module in the repo for money-handling discipline. Four things put it at the ceiling. (1) The atomic spend: verify every leg before touching a balance, deduct resources first and Cinder LAST with the ordering justified ("Cinder is the leg that can fail for reasons outside this function… unwinding N resource legs is cheaper and safer than unwinding a Cinder spend that has already fired a cloud write-through"), and `spendCost` hands its `refund` closure back to the caller on SUCCESS so a later record-failure can still unwind. (2) The refund bug, named and measured: "🔴 REFUND USES host.refundRes, NOT host.addRes. addRes enforces the stash cap and returns WITHOUT ADDING when the vault is full… A driven test caught exactly that: 95 metal and 70 supplies deducted, 'refunded', and gone." (3) The economy dial (`RESOURCE_COST_MULT` / `CINDER_COST_DIV`) applied at the single read point with the design argument written out — Cinder is farmable so pricing expansion in Cinder means farming buys expansion — plus "⚠ APPLIED HERE, NOT BAKED INTO THE 51 COST ENTRIES, on purpose. One knob to turn… so the UI and the spend can never disagree about the price." (4) Test seams that cannot leak: `simulateFailAt` "is a parameter rather than a global switch so no production call site can set it." It also handles the deliberate duplication of this grammar in index.html by bounding it and explaining why the alternative is impossible (index.html renders synchronously; a module is deferred by definition) — "If you change the grammar, change BOTH; there is a driven test for each." And `UNPRICED = 999999` with "an absent level stays unaffordable, never free."

Where the module set's defensive habits are densest. `ensureState()` is "🔴 ABSENT-TOLERANT ON LOAD. This project has shipped silent save bugs three times, so every field is defaulted and no shape is assumed." `HALT` gives every stop a distinct code and every branch returns a `reason` the UI must print PLUS a `fix` naming the concrete thing to go do — "An invisible halt reads as a bug" — and the ordering of the four checks is individually justified (staff first, because "an unstaffed building consumes nothing and should not be reported as short of inputs it never asked for"; brownout throttles to 0.4 so "a growing city degrades instead of falling off a cliff"). It states which system is the authority when two could disagree: "🔴 THE CAP REPORTED HERE IS THE LEDGER'S OWN CAP, NOT A LOCAL BELIEF", with the measured consequence of getting it wrong — a collect promised 810 food and banked 540, "270 units destroyed, clipped:false, and the 36h timer reset. Measured, not theorised." `collect()` measures what the ledger actually took rather than reporting the request, and advances the clock by the cycles actually PAID for. `record()` converts a `false` from the bridge into a throw precisely so `build()`'s refund path stays live, and `build()`'s ordering is fixed and argued: prereqs before cost, "the only order that is safe: refusing after spendCost() would mean refunding, and every refund path is a chance to hand back more than was taken." `chainRank`'s header states a rule about a data structure: "🔴 nothing here removes, reorders or rewrites a placed row. This project deleted paid-for buildings four rounds running; this function only READS the array."

The bar for data files: a catalog that argues for its own shape. It opens with the REJECTED design and calls it the point — "🔴 THIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED INTO CAMP_FACILITIES, and that is the whole design decision" — then names the three things that only look alike and the exact cost of merging them ("every facility read site… grew a 'but is it a factory?' branch"). It marks its own literals as provisional and pre-writes its own deletion: rates are "tuning starting points, NOT an authority… this comment exists to be deleted by whoever adds" a `_cityEcon()`. Array ORDER is documented as load-bearing with the player-experience reason (a Hydroponics Bay built first fills and stops, "which reads as a broken building rather than as a storage cap") and the instruction "Do not 'tidy' this into alphabetical order." A single entry documents a contradiction in its own spec and resolves it toward the stricter rule while explaining why the third leg is deliberately tiny. `CITY_PREREQ` records that the derived-from-inputs approach was rejected because "THE INPUT GRAPH HAS A CYCLE AND THIS TREE MUST NOT", and that only one level of depth is checked because transitivity is "enforced by construction rather than by walking the graph on every render." `missingPrereqs` accepts an Array, a Set or a count map because "every caller in the codebase holds a different one of those and none should have to convert." And `auditCatalog()` turns the spec's acceptance criteria into five runnable rules — exported but deliberately NOT run at import, "because a data assertion that throws on load would take the whole city down over a tuning typo" — with its own fallback id list carrying a staleness warning that explains how a stale list would invert the very bug the audit exists to catch.

The module-side half of the seam, and the shortest complete statement of the pattern (76 lines). It states WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL in terms of the language mechanic — lexical `const` bindings are not `window` properties, "`window.Profile` is undefined even though `const Profile` is right there" — names the two occasions it has already cost real time, and issues the standing instruction: "If a module needs something new from the legacy app, ADD IT TO THE BRIDGE (both here and in the index.html block that builds it). Do not reach around." `NULL_BRIDGE` is a full-shape no-op so the module can be imported, rendered, or tested with no game present, and `bridge()` duck-types one method (`typeof b.signedIn === 'function'`) rather than testing truthiness, so a half-built object is rejected rather than half-used. Even the utilities carry reasons: `esc()` is defined locally rather than imported from the legacy app "because every render path needs it and it must never be the reason a module fails to load", and `twNodes: () => []` is annotated with a design rule — objectives point at real Territory Wars nodes, so an empty return "says so rather than inventing targets."

The legacy-side bridge block, `window.MythicCityBridge` at lines 207415-207504 (read together with its header at 207333-207351 and the `MythicTradeBridge` banner at 207352-207372). This is the house style for a seam. Every accessor is a FUNCTION with the reason stated ("a captured value goes stale the moment the player loots or spends"); every method is try-wrapped and returns a typed default so nothing throws across the seam. It corrects the task doc it was built from, in place and loudly: "⚠ 🔴 RESOURCES DO NOT LIVE ON `Profile.resources`. The task doc asserts `Profile.resources?.[k]` and that is WRONG." It splits swallow-vs-report deliberately and says why, with the price attached: "🔴 RETURN FALSE ON FAILURE — DO NOT SWALLOW IT. These two were `try { … } catch (e) {}`, which made the module's refund-on-record-failure path dead code: a saveProfile() throw charged the player 50,000 Cinder for a building that never persisted, and build() still returned {ok:true}." `refundRes` vs `addRes` is distinguished as a safety property rather than a convenience. The idle contract is PASSED, never redeclared, "so production cannot become a third idle policy." `terroirSeed()` explains why the seed is the camp node rather than the account, and states the null case as an exact identity with pre-feature behaviour "which is what makes it safe to ship." And it leaves an honest, labelled dead hook: `outputMultipliers: null` with a note that the function was grepped for, does not exist, and how to wire it when it lands. The sibling `MythicTradeBridge` banner supplies the missing rationale for boolean mutators — a wrapper returning `undefined` on success "would make its rollback path fire on a leg that actually worked."

Renderers that are pure string builders — no DOM writes, no listeners (binding is a separate `bind(root)` in index.js, safe to call repeatedly) — with the two rules that drive every choice stated in the header, the second being "A halted building SAYS WHY, in the card, in words. An invisible halt reads as a bug and this project has shipped that mistake before." It carries WHY into the CSS itself: "🛑 The halt banner is deliberately loud. A stopped building that looks the same as a running one is the single most common 'the game is broken' report." Every failure state that `production.state.js` can produce has a corresponding visible banner (halt reason + `fix`, accrual cap, storage clip, input-limited cycles), the cost line shows every leg including unknown resource ids flagged with ⚠ rather than silently dropped, the empty state is an instruction ("start with the Warehouse") rather than a blank, and the stylesheet is exported for one-shot lazy injection by the entry module so a never-opened panel costs nothing.

The cleanest small module: one table, two consumers, and a header that declares up front which is which and that the resource share is "added ON TOP… it never taxes a player's existing yield." Its degradation contract is absolute and stated as a design requirement rather than an accident: "🔴 AND IT MUST DEGRADE TO NOTHING… An absent module must never change a payout. That is why every export is pure and total — no throws, no async, no I/O." Absence is given a real value, not null: "🆓 THE DEFAULT, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING", funnelled through one `resolve()` "so there is exactly one place that decides what 'no node' means." It records a rejected alternative with the operational reason: the admin override wins outright rather than taking a max, because "an admin must be able to move a node DOWN as well as up (a refund, a chargeback, a correction). Taking the max here would make demotion impossible and would be the harder bug to find later." Two node shapes are accepted on purpose so that "one resolver serves both call sites instead of two that can disagree about a player's rate." Representation choices are justified (rate stored as a percent because that is what the UI prints; the +1 named rather than inlined "because it is the one number most likely to be retuned"), omissions are documented (`scavenger` / `vault-key` "deliberately absent… rather than silently granting 1%"), and the sign is guarded because "a bug here that flipped the sign would quietly delete player output."

`spendGems()` / `addGems(amount, reason)` at lines 64429-64475 — the bar for editing a hot legacy function additively. The new `reason` parameter is optional "so all 29 existing callers are unchanged", and its justification is an audit argument with a production number: every faucet used to land in `wallet_ledger` as `addGems` or an anonymous reconcile blob, "so the Cinder supply could not be audited: production shows +602,357 🔥 of reconcile gains in one week with nothing attributing a single unit of it to a source. A named reason per faucet is the prerequisite for ever noticing abuse." Below it, the two-tables problem is stated as an authority conflict, not a bug report: `saveProgressCloud` writes `user_profiles.gems` while every server-authoritative spend reads `user_progress.cinder`, "so earnings accumulated in the profile mirror while the canonical row stayed near zero, and chargeCinderAtomic refused purchases the player could obviously afford (reported at client 661,147 vs server 1,143)." The fire-and-forget mirror is then justified conditionally — "Fire-and-forget is fine here ONLY because a failure marks the durable reconcile flag, which re-reads and lifts the server up later" — and the write-through is explained in terms of the player's experience ("Gem spend is one of the most upsetting things to lose") and the `beforeunload` guard it cooperates with.

The cloud-sync halves for `__convoy__` and `__cityProduction__` — upload payload at 46644-46683, hydration merge at 48007-48035. This is the repo at its best on a class of bug rather than an instance of one. The upload side names the trap on the key itself ("Profile.* is NOT synced automatically; a key only travels if it is named here AND read back in the hydration block. Without both halves a signed contract would quietly vanish on the next device") and then counts the recurrence: "🔴 THIS KEY IS THE FIFTH SILENT-SAVE BUG THIS PROJECT HAS SHIPPED, and it was caught before release only because it was audited… A player who spent 120,000 Cinder on a Gene Vault watched it vanish on their next device. See the __convoy__ note above — same trap, same file." The hydration side does not merge by habit; it states a MERGE POLICY per field with a distinct reason for each half — `owned` is a UNION because "a truck is bought with Aza (real money); a stale cloud copy must never be able to take one away", while `usedToday` is MAX-for-the-same-day because taking the lower number "would let a player dodge the daily cap just by switching devices, which is the exact farming this feature exists to stop", and a differing `dayKey` means the day rolled over so the local zero wins. Paid things union; anti-farm counters take the max; and the asymmetry is the design.

`GARAGE_RIG_FX` / `GARAGE_RIGS` / `_garageRig()` at 164185-164250, read with `_jbConvoys()` at 218935-219028. Together they are the model for a real-money feature living inside legacy code. Authority is declared twice, in both directions: "🚨 DISPLAY ONLY. GARAGE_RIGS in worker.js is the pricing authority and is what Stripe actually charges. If these two disagree the player is shown one price and billed another, so they must be changed together"; and "⚙ THE EFFECTS TABLE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH… the store's bullet points are GENERATED from it — so the shop can never advertise a number the engine does not deliver" — which `_rigPerks()` then actually implements, so the marketing copy is derived rather than duplicated. `_garageRig()` returns a neutral `{ owned:false, name:'Hand-hauled', load:1, risk:0, speed:1, tier:0 }` from both the no-rig path and the `catch`, "so every caller can use the same shape without branching on ownership" — the same object shape is the failure mode. It unions cash ownership with legacy Aza ownership so a pre-migration buyer "keeps the full benefit rather than only the daily-cap half of it." `_jbConvoys()` is then a pure function of the clock deliberately, "so there is nothing to store, nothing to tick, and two observers always agree", reads the rig once per call "so every convoy in a batch agrees", applies the risk cut BEFORE the clamp "so it still helps on a route that would otherwise be pinned at the ceiling", and returns `[]` on any throw.

pieces.title: sql/038 — transport schema, RLS, definer helpers and the four RPCs
pieces.goal: Write ONE new file, /home/user/Playmythicspellbook/sql/038_transport_companies.sql, that creates the four transport tables with their RLS in the same file, the SECURITY DEFINER ownership helper, a single-row config table for the server-owned ceilings, and the four RPCs transport_quote / transport_dispatch / transport_settle / transport_repair. It must be idempotent and re-runnable, must state its own status honestly at the top (it has NEVER been run — there is no CLI login in this repo and migrations are pasted by hand into the Supabase SQL editor for project ktsiasyjusesawtrwrjc), and must end with a counted verify query containing at least one NEGATIVE assertion. It is the entire security boundary for a feature where one player pays another player real Cinder, so the header must argue the boundary line by line and must publish the limit of what it can actually guarantee.
acceptance: File exists at sql/038_transport_companies.sql. It is the ONLY file added; there is no RUN_038_*.sql (RUN_* files are hand-paste bundles, not a parallel series) and no 016/038b.

Header states STATUS honestly (never run, applied by hand, what applying it does and does not achieve) and contains a 🔒 SECURITY REVIEW block that names, per bullet, the attack each measure closes — not what the measure does.

Header contains a section stating the LIMIT of the guarantee: what the server cannot check here (e.g. cargo the client claims to hold lives in Profile.salvage, a client blob; the server can bound and address a settlement but cannot recompute the shipper's inventory) with an explicit 'Do not read this file as claiming otherwise.'
Exactly four data tables + one config table, each with `create table if not exists`, each followed by `alter table … enable row level security` IN THIS FILE. grep proves 5 enable-RLS statements.

`public.is_transport_owner(p_company_id uuid)` exists as `language sql stable security definer set search_path = public`, takes the company id and answers about auth.uid() only — never takes a user id. Followed by `revoke all on function public.is_transport_owner(uuid) from public, anon;` and `grant execute … to authenticated;`.
For each table T, `grep -A8 "create policy .* on public.T"` does NOT mention T inside the policy body. No self-referential policy anywhere.
`using (true)` appears at most on transport_companies (the public rate board) and carries a comment saying it is a public directory. It appears on none of rigs / contracts / ledger / config.
transport_contracts SELECT policy names BOTH sides: `shipper_id = auth.uid()` OR `public.is_transport_owner(carrier_id)`. A policy expressing only one side fails.

NO UPDATE policy exists on transport_rigs or transport_companies, and `revoke update on public.transport_rigs from anon, authenticated;` + the same for transport_companies are present, with a comment explaining that Postgres RLS has no column granularity so a row-level UPDATE policy would also hand over runs_used / day_key / reliability / status.

transport_ledger has NO balance/total/earnings column. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy on it, plus `revoke insert, update, delete on public.transport_ledger from anon, authenticated;` and (if the PK is bigserial) `revoke all on sequence public.transport_ledger_id_seq from anon, authenticated;`. Balance is read as `coalesce(sum(amount),0)` everywhere.
transport_ledger.amount carries a sign/kind CHECK constraint added via drop-if-exists + add constraint, with a comment naming the negative-row-poisons-an-append-only-table attack.

Every RPC is `security definer` WITH `set search_path = public` (or `public, pg_temp`), and each is followed immediately by `revoke all on function public.NAME(<exact arg types>) from public, anon;` and `grant execute on function public.NAME(<exact arg types>) to authenticated;`. Argument types are spelled out in full.

No RPC takes a price, an amount, a user id, a reliability or a runs_used from the caller. transport_dispatch takes ids only and re-reads company / tariff / rig / depot / cap from the rows. transport_settle takes a contract id only.

The runs/day increment is a single statement whose WHERE clause is the concurrency guard, e.g. `update … set runs_used = case when day_key = v_today then runs_used + 1 else 1 end, day_key = v_today where id = … and (day_key <> v_today or runs_used < v_cap) returning true into v_ok;` followed by a refusal when v_ok is null. A read-then-write without `for update` fails.

day_key is computed from the DATABASE clock inside the function (e.g. `to_char((now() at time zone 'utc')::date,'YYYY-MM-DD')`), never taken as a parameter, with a comment saying why the client's getTodayKey() cannot be the authority.

The Meridian ceiling (2.5× median player tariff, 1.6× trip time) is read from the single-row config table inside transport_quote/transport_dispatch, not written as a scattered literal, and the tariff cap is enforced server-side.
Every RPC returns `jsonb_build_object('ok', …)` with a distinct `error` code string per refusal, and a not-authenticated branch returning `'not_authenticated'`.

Retry safety is explicit: dispatching or settling twice is harmless and says so (a unique index used as the retry guard, or an already-handled branch that returns the existing row rather than erroring), with a comment naming the double-click / dropped-connection case.

Ends with a verify query preceded by `-- Expect: …` naming counts the author actually counted, including at least one NEGATIVE assertion such as `(select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname='public' and tablename='transport_rigs' and cmd='UPDATE') as no_rig_upd` expected 0, and a ledger-has-no-write-policy check.
Re-runnable: pasting the whole file twice produces no error. Every create policy has a preceding `drop policy if exists`; every constraint has a preceding `alter table … drop constraint if exists`.
No `wallet_credit` call anywhere in the file (grep returns 0). No pg_net / net.http_post / outbound HTTP. No 'discord' or 'webhook' anywhere including comments.

pieces.title: rigs.data.js — the haul-class rig catalog and its runs/cargo maths
pieces.goal: Write ONE new file, /home/user/Playmythicspellbook/public/src/transport/rigs.data.js: the six-entry PP_RIGS catalog (one per existing game rarity), the weighted roll that puts a haul-class listing on the Prince Portfolios auction floor, the effective-runs maths (rarity runs × condition multiplier, floored at 1), the Garage-tier fleet perk mapping, and a runnable self-audit. It is a data file that must argue for its own shape: why the rig table sits BESIDE PP_VEHICLE_NAMES rather than inside it, why rarity for a rig comes from the entry rather than from condition, why lotSlots is authored but deliberately not enforced in v1, and which numbers are provisional. Pure and total: no I/O, no imports of anything but nothing at all, no bridge, no window reads at module scope, nothing that can throw at import.
acceptance: File exists at public/src/transport/rigs.data.js and `node --check public/src/transport/rigs.data.js` passes. (Do NOT cite `node _synckcheck.mjs` on a .js path — it only extracts inline <script> blocks from HTML, finds zero matches, prints ALL CLEAN and exits 0. That is a false green.)

Exports EXACTLY these names with these arities: PP_RIGS, PP_RIGS_BY_ID, RIG_RARITIES, rollRig(), rigById(id), rarityIndex(rarityId), effectiveRuns(rigId, condition, garageTier), fleetSlotBonus(garageTier), runsPerDayBonus(garageTier), auditRigs(rarityIds, condMult).

PP_RIGS has 6 entries whose `rarity` values are exactly the six lowercase ids from index.html's RARITIES: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, mythic. No parallel ladder, no capitalised keys, no 'Uncommon'-less five-tier set.
